mnemonic: A chalk line on the floor: this side, yes; that side, not happening.
meaning: to draw a line: to rule something out firmly, or to keep someone at a distance
usage: Two common uses: (1) in the news, an official firmly denying or ruling out a possibility (~ 가능성에 선을 그었다); (2) in relationships, keeping someone at arm's length (그는 나와 선을 그었다). Neutral.

examples.ko: 정부는 추가 증세 가능성에 대해 분명히 선을 그었다.
examples.en: The government firmly ruled out further tax increases.

examples.ko: 친하게 지내고 싶었는데 걔가 먼저 선을 긋더라.
examples.en: I wanted us to be close, but she drew a line first.

cloze.en: The company firmly ruled out the possibility of restructuring.
cloze.cue: drew a firm line (ruled it out), past tense

nearMiss.hint: Also natural (stating something firmly to settle it), but the cue is after another word.

mnemonic: A bucket of cold water over a warm party: the fun stops instantly.
meaning: to throw cold water on (a mood or plans); to dampen spirits
usage: For a remark, event, or person that kills enthusiasm or spoils a good atmosphere: 분위기에 찬물을 끼얹다, or in economic news, 회복세에 찬물을 끼얹다. Also 찬물 끼얹는 소리 ('a wet-blanket remark').

examples.ko: 모처럼 살아나던 소비 심리에 금리 인상이 찬물을 끼얹었다.
examples.en: The rate hike threw cold water on consumer sentiment just as it was finally reviving.

examples.ko: 다들 신났는데 찬물 끼얹는 소리 좀 하지 마.
examples.en: Everyone's excited, so don't be such a wet blanket.

cloze.sentence: 다들 들떠 있는데 굳이 {{}} 필요는 없잖아.
cloze.en: Everyone's so excited; there's no need to go throwing cold water on it.
cloze.cue: throw cold water on things (modifier form, before 'no need to')

nearMiss.hint: Also fits (spoil the fun), but the cue is after another word.

mnemonic: 隔 separated + 世 generation + 之 of + 感 feeling: you feel a whole generation away from your own past.
meaning: the feeling that times have changed drastically; feeling like it's a different world
literal: the feeling of being a generation removed
usage: Used when comparing past and present, especially about rapid social or technological change: 격세지감을 느끼다. Neutral; frequent in essays and interviews, and in conversation when people look back.

examples.ko: 삼십 년 전 공중전화 앞에 줄 서던 시절을 떠올리면 격세지감을 느낀다.
examples.en: Thinking back thirty years to lining up for pay phones, it feels like a different world.

examples.ko: 요즘 애들은 태어날 때부터 스마트폰을 쓰니까 진짜 격세지감이야.
examples.en: Kids these days use smartphones from birth. Times have really changed.

production.promptEn: the feeling that times have changed drastically (lit. a generation removed)

mnemonic: 針 needle + 小 small + 棒 club + 大 big: a needle's worth of fact, a club's worth of story.
meaning: blowing something out of proportion; exaggerating a small matter
literal: making a needle into a club
usage: Critical; about exaggeration in the media, rumors, or arguments: 침소봉대하다, 사실을 침소봉대해 보도하다.

examples.ko: 일부 언론이 사소한 말실수를 침소봉대해 큰 논란으로 만들었다.
examples.en: Some outlets blew a minor slip of the tongue out of proportion into a major controversy.

examples.ko: 그 정도 일 가지고 침소봉대하지 마.
examples.en: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill over something like that.

accepted: make a mountain out of a molehill

production.promptEn: blowing something out of proportion (lit. making a needle into a club)

mnemonic: A loose stone tumbles downhill and knocks the old, settled one right out of its socket.
meaning: a newcomer pushes out the old-timer
literal: a stone that rolled in dislodges the stone that was embedded
usage: Said, often resentfully, when a newcomer displaces someone established: at work, on a team, in a family business. Often quoted or clipped: 굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼는 격이다.

examples.ko: 입사한 지 석 달 된 경력직이 팀장이 되자 다들 굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 뺀다고 수군댔다.
examples.en: When an experienced hire who'd been there three months became team leader, people muttered about newcomers pushing out the old guard.

examples.ko: 새로 온 사람이 내 자리를 차지하다니, 굴러온 돌이 박힌 돌 빼는 꼴이네.
examples.en: The new guy taking my spot: talk about the newcomer pushing out the old-timer.

accepted: newcomer pushes out the old timer
the newcomer pushes out the old guard

mnemonic: Even the dead have a story about why it wasn't their fault.
meaning: everyone has an excuse for everything
literal: there's no grave without an excuse
usage: Wry or exasperated, about people who always have a reason for failing or being late: 핑계 없는 무덤 없다더니. Even the dead have an excuse for dying.

examples.ko: 핑계 없는 무덤 없다더니, 지각할 때마다 이유도 가지가지네.
examples.en: Everyone's got an excuse, as they say: every time you're late, there's a brand-new reason.

examples.ko: 실패한 사업가들의 인터뷰를 읽다 보면 핑계 없는 무덤 없다는 말이 절로 떠오른다.
examples.en: Reading interviews with failed entrepreneurs, you can't help recalling that every grave has its excuse.

accepted: everybody has an excuse for everything
